cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Fraudulent – obtained, done by, or involving deception, especially criminal deception.

p.em: Example: The bank warned its customers about a series of fraudulent emails asking for passwords.

cosy-blockquote.p: Verification – the process of establishing the truth, accuracy, or validity of something.

p.em: Example: Two-step verification is an essential security measure for protecting your online accounts.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the fact of being who or what a person or thing is.

p.em: Example: Digital identity theft can take months or even years to fully resolve.

cosy-blockquote.p: Phishing – the fraudulent practice of sending emails to induce individuals to reveal personal information.

p.em: Example: He realized the message was a phishing attempt when he noticed the suspicious URL.
Example: Always check for the blue checkmark to ensure that a celebrity's profile is authentic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerability ≠ resilience – state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed.

p.em: Example: Recognizing our structural vulnerability online is the first step toward cybersecurity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Credential – a qualification, achievement, personal quality, or aspect of a person's background.

p.em: Example: You should never share your login credentials with anyone, even if they claim to be from tech support.

cosy-blockquote.p: Malicious – intending or intended to do harm.

p.em: Example: Malicious software can infect your computer through a single suspicious download.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pretext – a reason given in justification of a course of action that is not the real reason.

p.em: Example: The scammer contacted him under the pretext of needing help with a charity donation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Surveillance – close observation of individuals or networks for security.

p.em: Example: Constant surveillance is a threat to the fundamental human right to privacy.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to cybersecurity research, what specific parameters characterize a highly structured and fraudulent digital profile?
★ Have you ever received a highly suspicious request or connection on LinkedIn or social media?

What empirical evidence shows that standard trust verification badges can be bypassed using automated web bots?
★ How carefully do you check the spelling and email address of messages from your bank?

Based on clinical behavioral data, how does the trauma of digital identity theft damage a victim's real-world social trust scores?
★ What is your reaction when you see a celebrity promoting a product? Do you check if the account is verified?

What parameters make a modern automated phishing campaign significantly harder to identify than simple spam filters?
★ Do you use a password manager or follow strict security rules for your credentials?

What biometric indicators are researchers using to prove a remote speaker's streams are authentic?
★ Have you ever had your email, social profile, or personal identity compromised?

According to behavioral studies, what psychological vulnerability is targeted most effectively by fake support profiles?
★ Who do you think is most vulnerable to digital scams in your family or community?

What technical weaknesses allow a malicious script to harvest a user's master credential folder?
★ What is the most convincing email phishing attempt you have ever personally spotted?

How does the paper differentiate simple profile scraping from highly targeted, malicious deepfake video scams?
★ Do you feel that online networks like LinkedIn have become less authentic recently?

Based on cognitive research, why is an urgent financial emergency the most successful social engineering pretext?
★ Would you change your daily habits if you knew scammers were watching your public profile?

What data metrics prove that intensive server-side network surveillance can prevent identity fraud without violating user privacy?
★ What digital safety habits do you talk about most with your close friends?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to track polymorphic cyberattacks, all fraudulent accounts will eventually be eliminated by advanced server-side AI detectors.
★ Would you trust an AI-led automated security system to manage all your personal accounts?

As our understanding of biometric verification models develops, continuous retinal scanning will be the only standard method to access public domains.
★ Would you support mandatory biometric scans (like retina or fingerprint) for all social media accounts?

Imagine future research proves that digital identity is a fundamental biological right; global treaties will enforce heavy criminal sentences for cloning personal digital twins.
★ Do you think social media platforms should be legally liable for scam accounts on their sites?

If we map targeted social phishing models using neural simulators, user systems will automatically neutralize conversational pretext attacks before they reach human view.
★ How do you think digital identity theft will change when deepfakes become perfect?

Imagine future research shows that authentic human voices have unique electromagnetic frequencies; synthetic vocal channels will be easily filtered out in real time.
★ Would you pay a monthly fee for absolute identity security on a public platform?

If we can measure psychological vulnerability using biometric watches, the user's interface will automatically lock login panels during high-cortisol states.
★ Should digital literacy be a required course for graduation in every school?

As cryptographic protocols evolve, every digital credential will be updated continuously in milliseconds to guarantee invulnerability.
★ If your digital twin could answer emails and do boring work for you, would you want one?

Imagine future research shows that malicious scripts are targeting specific auditory nerves; holographic headsets will be banned for general consumer use.
★ Do you feel secure using fingerprint or facial recognition on your phone?

If developers automate the identification of any deceptive pretext, scammers will be forced to return to physical real-world crimes.
★ What makes real-world face-to-face interaction feel safer and more authentic to you?

As security concerns mount, intensive public surveillance networks will replace private local area networks globally.
★ Are you worried about your personal privacy in an era of constant online surveillance?

ul.li: Incorrect: They have stole my identity → Correct: They have stolen my identity ((Irregular past participle))
Incorrect: It is a fraud account → Correct: It is a fraudulent account / a fake account ((Noun vs Adjective))
Incorrect: I am careful with my passwords since always → Correct: I have always been careful with my passwords ((Present Perfect + Frequency adverb))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
